title: Korean War Original Artwork for Propaganda Leaflet & Original Leaflet (한국전쟁삐라와 원그림) 2점
desc_orig: Rare original pen and ink art   for a propaganda leaflet that was created to be dropped on Chinese and North Korean troops. The artwork features a giant United Nations officer standing in front of a United Nations flag and looking down at two obviously frightened Chinese officers who cling to his arm as they look across a chasm where the Grim Reaper, in Pied Piper of Hamelin fashion, is leading Chinese troops over the edge where the skeletons of their comrades await them. A row of cannon barrels flank the U.N. officer.   The propaganda leaflet was copied from this pen & ink drawing. Chinese characters were added to the officer's sleeve. The back of the paper leaflet greets the Chinese troops, "We are the United Nations troops in North Korea, different countries. We welcome you!!.. ....and then goes on to proclaim that the U.N.troops hold no grudges against the Chinese officers and men but have to treat them as enemies and fight them ....."the saying goes: Treat a friend like a friend! As treat an enemy like an enemy! . This drawing has not been removed from the frame. The visible part measures "16.25" x 10.25" and is housed in a 24.5" x 18.5 frame. The paper propaganda leaflet measures 7.5" x 5".     In-house shipping is available. desc_orig: Flyer published by the General Political Bureau of the Korean People's Army dropped over American and British soldiers during the Korean War encouraging the troops to surrender and support a world peace pact, approx. 10 x 7 inches. Graphic on obverse of a dead Korean person amongst a destroyed landscape titled, 'Even Hitler the civilized savage will shrink from such barbarism as this!'. Verso has an appeal from prisoners of war imprisoned by the Korean Army to the United States, the Soviet Union, China, the United Kingdom, and France to sign a peace pact and end the Korean War, 'We the undersigned prisoners of war...send this voluntary appeal directly to the five great powers...to sign a peace pact at the first opportunity to preserve world peace...We feel that time must not be lost in the signing of a peace treaty...with the understanding that any one of the above which refuses to attend conferences, for the purpose of constructing a peace pact, is to be considered a government with aggressive intentions.' The flyer then lists 30 printed signatures of prisoners of war. Flyer faded, slight damage and loss on edges, minor tears, minor loss on folds, and mailing folds.

maker: published by the International Union of Students (IUS), Country of issue: Czechoslovakia
desc_orig: Original vintage political propaganda poster titled U. S., HANDS OFF SOUTH KOREA!, published by the International Union of Students (IUS). This striking and historically significant poster features a bold graphic of a US military police officer MP in a helmet, depicted in a minimalist, almost skeletal style. He is shown walking past a red-and-white barrier with a large, circular STOP sign, symbolising the demand to halt American military presence in the region. The background consists of a bright green map of the Korean peninsula set against a solid light-blue sky. The composition is framed by powerful typography, with the title in bold black at the top. At the bottom, the dates 1950.6.25 and 1963.6.25 mark the 13th anniversary of the start of the Korean War, emphasising a long-standing call for solidarity and an end to foreign intervention. Produced by the IUS, an organisation that was central to coordinating global student support for anti-imperialist movements, this piece is an excellent example of international political graphic design from the early 1960s. Fair condition, folds, creasing, tears, pinholes, tape on edges, small paper losses, paper skimming. Country of issue: Czechoslovakia, designer: Unknown, size (cm): 40.5x29, year of printing: 1963.

title: 삐라: 명령. Order. Life in the P.O.W. Camps., Korean War Leaflet -Kim Il-Sung's "Policy of Leniency" (김일성 싸인)
desc_orig: Black and white photographic illustrations. 8 x 10.5cm. Leaflet faintly foxed and trifle creased, overall in very good condition. A propaganda leaflet issued by the North Korean regime for United Nations forces, encouraging surrender and cooperation with the Korean People's Army and People's Volunteer Army.The leaflet outlines Kim Il-sung's "policy of leniency", and assures that captured prisoners of war will be guaranteed "security of life, retention of all personal belongings, freedom from maltreatment or abuse, and medical care if wounded or ill". Carefully staged photographs of POWs occupying themselves with recreation punctuate the leaflet, implying an idyllic existence vastly improved over active warfare. In truth, the experiences of POWs was invariably harsh and unforgiving, particularly during the winter. While sources confirm that the Chinese treatment of POWs was markedly better than the treatment afforded by the North Koreans, there remain several POW accounts indicating a persistent implied threat of violence, and a widespread disregard of the Geneva Convention.
